title: Hiking Hells Gate in a Day: Fischer's Tower, the Gorge and the Road From Nairobi
meta_title: Hells Gate Hike: A Spectacular 16 km Gorge Walk Near Nairobi
meta_description: Plan your Hells Gate hike: the 16 km route from Elsa Gate to the gorge, getting there from Nairobi, flash-flood safety, best months and what to pack.
excerpt: A Hells Gate hike covers about 16-17 km from Elsa Gate to the Ol Njorowa Gorge and back. Here is how to get there from Nairobi, the route, the flood risk and what to pack.
content:
Eight kilometres of gravel between red cliffs separate Elsa Gate from the gorge, and that stretch is most of a Hells Gate hike. Walk it out and back to the Lower Gorge and you cover about 16-17 km in 5-6 hours, starting at roughly 1,900 m in Hells Gate National Park near Lake Naivasha.

The park sits about 90 km north-west of Nairobi, close enough for a day out from the city. Below: getting there by car or matatu, the route past Fischer's Tower, when the gorge floods, what to wear and the mistakes first-timers make.

Hells Gate at a Glance

  • Location: Hells Gate National Park, Nakuru County, on the south side of Lake Naivasha, about 90 km from Nairobi.
  • Main route: about 8 km from Elsa Gate to the Ol Njorowa Gorge, so a Hells Gate hike there and back is 16-17 km.
  • Time: 5-6 hours walking, plus 1-2 hours if you go down into the Lower Gorge with a guide.
  • Gate hours: 6:00am to 6:00pm, according to KWS.
  • Driest months: roughly June-October and January-February; flash-flood risk peaks in the March-May long rains.

Where Is Hells Gate and How Do You Get There From Nairobi?

Hells Gate National Park lies in the floor of the Rift Valley, just south of Lake Naivasha in Nakuru County. The park covers about 68 km² and was gazetted in 1984. From Nairobi CBD it is roughly 90 km, usually 2-2.5 hours by car with traffic.

Plenty of people treat the Hells Gate hike as a long day trip. Leave Nairobi by 6:00am and you can be walking from Elsa Gate before the heat builds on a road with very little shade.

Which road should you drive?

Two routes work. One follows the A104 through Limuru and Uplands to Naivasha, then Moi South Lake Road. The other drops down the old escarpment road through Mai Mahiu, past the foot of Mt Longonot. Both reach the signed Elsa Gate turning; KWS directions describe the gate as about 25 km along from the Moi South Lake Road junction.

Can you get to Hells Gate by matatu?

Yes, though a Hells Gate hike by public transport takes longer. Naivasha matatus leave from the River Road and Nyamakima area of Nairobi CBD; confirm the stage with a conductor. In Naivasha town, take a matatu along Moi South Lake Road towards Olkaria and get off at the Elsa Gate junction, about 2 km from the gate on foot or by boda boda. Matatus leave when full, so allow an extra hour for the return.

The Hells Gate Hike, Section by Section

The classic route follows the main access road from Elsa Gate to the gorge, then drops into the Lower Gorge with a guide.

Elsa Gate to Fischer's Tower

Within the first couple of kilometres of a Hells Gate hike, the road passes Fischer's Tower, a volcanic plug about 25 m tall that climbers know as Oloroka in Maa. The narrow break in the cliffs here gave the park its name. Watch for vultures and Verreaux's eagles above the rock.

The open valley towards Central Tower

After Fischer's Tower the valley widens into grassland. Here you are most likely to see zebra, eland, Thomson's gazelle, hartebeest and buffalo grazing near the road. Keep well clear of buffalo. Steam from the Olkaria geothermal plants rises on the horizon; Olkaria I opened in 1981.

Central Tower, a second volcanic plug, marks the head of the gorge. The 14 km Buffalo Circuit loop also passes it, giving you another way back. On a Hells Gate hike at a steady pace, most walkers reach the gorge picnic area and ranger post about two hours after leaving Elsa Gate.

Into the Ol Njorowa Gorge

The Lower Gorge is a narrow slot of water-carved rock with warm streams fed by hot springs. Expect rock steps, tight bends and wet feet. A KWS ranger or an authorised community guide is required for this section, and bicycles are not allowed in it. Guides usually offer short, medium and long loops.

Is the Hells Gate Hike Safe in the Rainy Season?

The road walk is safe in most weather, but the gorge is not. Flash floods have killed visitors twice in recent memory: seven members of a church group in April 2012, and six tourists and their guide in September 2019. Water can surge through the gorge when rain falls near Mt Longonot, even under blue sky.

In November the short rains are under way around Naivasha, which makes the timing of a Hells Gate hike matter, and the long rains of roughly March to May bring the highest risk. If cloud is building to the south, or your guide hesitates, skip the Lower Gorge. For more on wet-weather walking, read our notes on hiking safely when the rain comes in.

When is the best time to hike Hells Gate?

June to October and January to February are the most reliable months for a Hells Gate hike. The ground is dry and the rock less slippery. Whatever the month, start by 8:00am, because the valley heats up fast and the return is a gradual climb.

What to Wear and Pack for a Hells Gate Hike

Dress for sun on the road and grip in the gorge. That means a broad-brimmed hat, a light long-sleeved shirt, at least 2-3 litres of water each and footwear with a sticky, deep-lugged sole that you do not mind getting wet.

Footwear: boots, trail shoes or sandals?

The gravel road on a Hells Gate hike is fine in trainers, but the gorge rewards proper grip. A light hiking boot such as the Quechua MH100 hiking boots holds well on the rock steps and dries out reasonably fast. Sandals tempt people in the streams, but volcanic rock is hard on bare toes. Read our guide to boots for Kenyan trails if you are choosing a pair.

Water, sun and rain cover

There is nowhere to buy water once a Hells Gate hike begins, so a 3L camel hydration backpack is the easiest way to carry enough and keep drinking while you walk. Pair it with a wide-brim safari sun hat, sunscreen and sunglasses. In November or April, add a waterproof rain poncho for afternoon storms.

A small 28L day hiking backpack holds all of that plus snacks and a dry pair of socks for the car. Pro Tips for Hells Gate

  • Book or meet your Lower Gorge guide at the gorge ranger post, and agree the loop and fee before you set off.
  • Keep food zipped away near the picnic sites, where baboons are bold.
  • Turn back from the gorge at the first sign of heavy cloud to the south, towards Longonot.
  • If you cycle in, check the brakes and tyres before you pay.
  • Confirm current park fees, guide rules and opening times with KWS before you travel.

How Hard Is the Hells Gate Hike for Beginners?

For most reasonably active people, Hells Gate is one of the gentler full days near Nairobi. The road has no steep climbs, and the gorge loops are short. The real challenges are distance, heat and the scrambling in the Lower Gorge.

If 10 km is your longest walk so far, break up your first Hells Gate hike by hiring a bike for the road and saving your legs for the gorge. Cyclists cover the 8 km in under an hour each way. Fit hikers wanting more can pair the park with nearby Mt Longonot and its crater rim on a separate day.

Common mistakes on a first Hells Gate hike

  1. Starting at 10:00am and walking back uphill in the midday heat.
  2. Carrying one 500 ml bottle for a 16 km day.
  3. Entering the gorge on a cloudy afternoon in the rains to save time.
  4. Wearing smooth-soled fashion trainers that skid on wet rock.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does the Hells Gate hike take?

The Hells Gate hike from Elsa Gate to the gorge and back takes most walkers 5-6 hours on foot, covering about 16-17 km. Add 1-2 hours for a guided loop in the Lower Gorge and time for breaks. Cycling the road section cuts the total to roughly half a day, which is why many visitors hire a bike near the gate.

Do you need a guide at Hells Gate?

You need a guide for the Ol Njorowa Gorge. Park rules require visitors to go into the Lower Gorge with a ranger or an authorised community guide, mainly because of the flash-flood risk. The roads, Fischer's Tower and the Buffalo Circuit can be walked or cycled without one. Guide fees change, so confirm them at the ranger post before you start.

Can I do a Hells Gate hike in November?

You can hike Hells Gate in November, but plan around the short rains. Mornings are often clear, with storms building in the afternoon, so start early and keep the gorge for a dry day. If rain has fallen near Longonot or your guide advises against it, walk the open road and towers instead and leave the gorge for another visit.

Is it better to cycle or walk at Hells Gate?

Cycling is better if you are short on time or not used to 16 km walks, because the 8 km road to the gorge takes under an hour by bike. Walking is better for watching wildlife and birds up close. Many people cycle to the gorge, then explore the Lower Gorge on foot with a guide.

How much does it cost to enter Hells Gate National Park?

Hells Gate entry fees depend on residency, age and season, and Kenya Wildlife Service reviews them from time to time, so we do not quote a figure here. Check the current rates on the Kenya Wildlife Service park page or at Elsa Gate before you travel. Budget separately for the gorge guide and any bike hire.

Final Thoughts

Two hours from the city, Hells Gate gives you red cliffs, grazing zebra and a hot-spring gorge in a single day on foot. Start early, carry more water than feels sensible and respect the weather before you step into the Lower Gorge. That is the whole secret of a good Hells Gate hike.

Pick a dry morning, sort out boots with real grip and a hydration pack, then check our hike calendar if you want company.
